task_specification.objective: Make hostile warnings readable at 25–40-enemy density, restore authoritative pause and terminal input ownership, and deliver a bounded, observable dense-run rendering workload ready for native 1920×1080 qualification while preserving accepted combat, teardown, weapons, registry, and cemetery systems.

diagnosis.root_cause: Three ownership defects remain. Ordinary enemies independently render full-strength emissive telegraphs, so simultaneous warnings accumulate over the Warden and escape lanes. Always-processing ancestry permits gameplay and wave simulation during pause, while Result-to-Title clears its action latch before input ownership safely transfers. Dense-run qualification also lacks native representative and retry evidence; the candidate compounds rendering risk with an always-on RoleGlow per active ordinary enemy, although the accepted neighbor registry is already bounded.

stop_conditions: Do not schedule or modify the deferred camera-occlusion, primitive-presentation, animation-binding, or semantic-audio issues.

Do not change enemy damage, attack ranges, legal targeting, weapon behavior, authored animation bindings, or the accepted one-rebuild-per-physics-frame and 12-candidate neighbor registry to obtain a visual or performance pass.
Stop the telegraph treatment if any damage-capable attack can advance without an attributable pre-damage cue or admission state survives death, pool return, teardown, or retry.
Stop the pause treatment if Title, Pause, Settings, Upgrade Draft, Result, or terminal cleanup loses input responsiveness while gameplay is made pausable.
If a representative native renderer is unavailable, retain candidate instrumentation but do not claim the dense-performance check passed or tune unrelated systems from llvmpipe results.
Developer self-validation does not close issues or phase checks; formal recapture, verdicts, and closure remain Host/Tester-owned.

strategy.rationale: Repair each defect at its authoritative boundary: encounter-owned warning admission instead of repeated per-instance tuning, explicit pause/input ownership instead of scattered guards, and deterministic ordinary-enemy lighting budgets plus density receipts instead of rewriting the preserved neighbor registry.

code: Developer: import and boot the native Godot project with no fatal or recurring GDScript/runtime errors; verify every changed scene and resource loads with its actual runtime binding.

Inspect scene process ownership: controller and required shell nodes remain always-processing, while World and WaveDirector are explicitly pausable; verify no gameplay child override reintroduces always-process behavior.
Verify validation actions exist only behind the editor/release guard, remain absent from project.godot physical bindings and release controls, and keep preparation separate from gameplay advancement.

Regression-check the preserved 12-entry upgrade catalog, three weapon runtimes, EnemyNeighborRegistry one-rebuild/12-candidate bounds, stable-id/generation cleanup, authoritative teardown receipts, and intact authored cemetery instance.
runtime: Host/Tester: at the same Wave-4 camera framing, capture pre-action, peak, and recovery with 25–40 ordinary enemies and all three weapons. Bind the views to active-enemy count, role mix, cue-admission counters, damage events, and escape-lane visibility.

Host/Tester: pause ordinary active play, enter nested Settings, wait, and compare before/during snapshots for run time, wave state, live identities, health, boss/attack clocks, projectiles, and rewards; Resume must continue exactly once from the frozen state.

Host/Tester: prepare failure and victory Results separately, then exercise Return to Title with keyboard and gamepad. Require one action generation, one complete title teardown receipt, Play focus, quit_requested=false, and no Exit Game modal; also smoke Retry for clean state.

Host/Tester: on a native 1920×1080 renderer, sample 3, 5, 10, and 18 enemies, then profile the representative final wave and boss with 25–40 ordinary enemies, all three weapons, pickups, animation, VFX, lights, HUD, and audio. Record frame-time distribution and workload counters, then repeat three complete retries and require stable nodes, registry entries, signals, pools, dynamic lights, audio, ?
visual: Compare repaired dense combat with the supplied high-angle Mournlight reference language: the dark ground remains legible, warm Warden lighting anchors the player, hostile cues stay restrained, and actors plus an escape route remain readable.

Inspect dense-light selection across adjacent frames for flicker, popping, lost silhouettes, overbright clusters, or an unintentionally flat or dark arena; verify danger remains readable without color alone.

Capture Title, Settings, Pause, Upgrade Draft, failure Result, victory Result, and returned Title at 1920×1080 in windowed/fullscreen modes and supported UI scales; require full-viewport composition, valid focus, unclipped controls, and no unintended modal.

done_when: At deterministic Wave-4 density with 25–40 active enemies and all four ordinary roles, every damage event is preceded by its admitted ring or lane cue for the full declared telegraph interval; denied requests wait without advancing a hidden damage countdown, and the configured simultaneous high-salience cue cap is never exceeded.

Admission uses stable-id and spawn-generation ordering, reports requested, admitted, waiting, and released counts, and releases ownership on damage, escape, death, retirement, pool return, encounter reset, terminal teardown, and retry with zero stale owners afterward.

Same-framing pre-action, peak, and recovery views preserve the Warden and enemy silhouettes, distinguish hostile rings and ranged lanes from friendly weapon effects, and leave at least one readable escape lane at 25–40-enemy density.

Ordinary cue materials remain restrained against the cemetery floor: opacity, emission, width, growth, and vertical placement prevent stacked overbrightness while every admitted warning remains readable without color being its sole danger indicator.
tasks.instructions: Move simultaneous ordinary-enemy warning ownership into a deterministic encounter-level admission budget keyed by stable id and spawn generation. EnemyActor must obtain admission before starting its telegraph countdown; when capacity is unavailable, keep the actor in a safe waiting or approach state rather than hiding or shortening warning time. Preserve distinct ring and ranged-lane geometry, then restrain material opacity, emission, width, and growth. Expose admission state and lifecycle counters through the existing candidate snapshot surface. Preserve accepted movement, separation, damage, death/drop, pooling, semantic presentation, and authored cemetery bindings.
tasks.title: Bound hostile telegraph admission and overdraw

done_when: With Pause open and again inside nested Settings, tree_paused remains true while run elapsed time, wave id, wave phase/time, spawn totals, live stable-id/generation set, Warden health, boss clocks, attack serials, projectiles, and rewards remain unchanged across an observation interval; Resume continues the same state exactly once.

The run controller and shell remain responsive while World, WaveDirector, enemies, weapons, pickups, boss behavior, and gameplay clocks use explicit pausable ownership rather than inheriting always-process behavior from the root.

From both victory and failure Result, one keyboard confirm and one gamepad confirm on Return to Title each produce exactly one complete title teardown receipt, leave quit_requested false, show a clean Title with Play focused, and never open the Exit Game confirmation. The terminal action remains consumed until release and cannot activate the newly focused page.

Mouse, keyboard, and gamepad navigation still works across Title, Settings, Upgrade Draft, Pause, failure/victory Result, Retry, and Return to Title. Settings retain persisted audio, window, UI-scale, effect, danger-contrast, and target-bias values across retry and title transitions.
White-box state exposes current pause/process ownership and a terminal input-handoff generation or receipt so each black-box transition binds to exactly one authoritative action.
tasks.instructions: Separate always-processing orchestration and UI from pausable gameplay at the scene/process-mode boundary. Keep only the run controller and required shell/draft UI responsive during pause; explicitly make World and WaveDirector pausable and remove SurvivalFoundation's unconditional always-process override. Add a generation-aware terminal action handoff barrier so Result-to-Title performs teardown immediately but does not expose or focus the title component until the initiating confirm has been consumed and released. Preserve the authoritative teardown receipts, existing title component, settings store, truthful result summary, and retry path; do not edit imported or addon sources.
tasks.title: Restore pause and terminal input ownership

done_when: Ordinary-enemy RoleGlow and HurtLight work is governed by a configurable deterministic density budget. The snapshot reports requested, active, suppressed, and peak light counts; active counts never exceed declared caps, priority does not flicker between adjacent frames, and pooled or dead actors retain no light request or stale hurt pulse.

Budgeting affects only optional ordinary-enemy fill and hurt lighting: emissive role silhouettes, admitted danger cues, the Warden lantern, cemetery landmarks, boss warnings, hit causality, and enemy semantic states remain intact and readable.

Editor-only unbound preparation supports stable inspectable density checkpoints at 3, 5, 10, 18, and representative 25–40 enemies with the legal three-weapon build. Each preparation reports requested and resolved density, run serial, setup generation, active/pooled counts, light-budget counts, neighbor-registry counters, and reset isolation without advancing attacks or terminal state.
